title: Epic: Direct Garmin Connect API import (replace web/CSV import)
description:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)

- Requirement 1: After a successful CSV conversion, the app automatically uploads the new weight records to Garmin Connect via the unofficial DI OAuth2 API (wire contract of python-garminconnect 0.3.x). No browser/WebView in the happy path.
- Requirement 2: One-time interactive login: email/password + full MFA (code entry, code re-trigger). The app stores ONLY DI tokens (`di_token`, `di_refresh_token`, `di_client_id`) — never email/password — AES-encrypted with an Android Keystore key, persisted in SharedPreferences.
- Requirement 3: Each uploaded record carries weight + percent fat + BMI, encoded as a weight_scale FIT message built with the official Garmin `com.garmin.fit:fit` SDK, uploaded via multipart `POST connectapi.garmin.com/upload-service/upload`.
- Requirement 4: A local dedup journal of sent timestamps; records already present in the journal are skipped when the same CSV is shared again.
- Requirement 5: Any upload failure (no token / login failed or cancelled / 429 / 5xx after retries / transport / partial `detailedImportResult.failures`) produces a fallback CSV built ONLY from unuploaded records via the existing `GarminCsvSchema`, saved to Downloads, and opens the Garmin web import flow as today. No CSV is written on full success.
- Requirement 6: Login UI is an AlertDialog-based dialog (single activity, no fragments), reachable both from a "Connect Garmin" action on the main screen and auto-triggered when a CSV arrives with no valid token.
- Requirement 7: garmin.com domain only. Debug builds log full HTTP exchanges (TAG `GarminHttp`) with `Authorization`, `password`, `mfaVerificationCode`, and `refresh_token` redacted; release builds log nothing of the sort.
- Requirement 8: The existing conversion pipeline (`FileRepository.processCsvFile` and its test suite) remains functionally unchanged; upload lives in a separate repository.
- Requirement 9: New code follows repo conventions: `garmin/` package, per-class TAG logging in `companion object`, manual DI via `MainViewModelFactory.createInstance`, EN/RU strings kept in sync.
- Requirement 10: Unit tests per repo convention (one test class per new component), MockWebServer for HTTP clients, FIT encode→decode roundtrip test; no real network in unit tests.

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)

- [ ] Sharing a real Goodvibes CSV with a valid token uploads all new records; Garmin Connect shows weight + fat (BMI when accepted) with no manual step
- [ ] Re-sharing the same CSV uploads 0 new records (journal dedup) and reports "nothing new"
- [ ] With no token: the login dialog (including the MFA path) appears; after successful login the upload proceeds automatically
- [ ] On failure (offline / revoked token / 429): a fallback CSV containing only unuploaded records lands in Downloads and the browser import opens; already-uploaded records are not duplicated
- [ ] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` passes including the new `garmin/` test classes; `./gradlew lintDebug` is clean
- [ ] The live auth spike on a debug build is documented (pass/fail + redacted log excerpt) — the OkHttp-vs-Cloudflare TLS question has an answer
- [ ] No credential or token value appears in any log line, in any build

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO storing Garmin email/password on disk (security: only DI tokens, Keystore-encrypted; refresh must work without credentials)
- ❌ NO plaintext token storage and NO androidx.security/EncryptedSharedPreferences (security/maintenance: deprecated upstream; AES key must come from Android Keystore)
- ❌ NO retrying 429 or auth errors (abuse/ratelimit: 429 → immediate fallback; auth failure → LoginRequired state, never a relogin loop)
- ❌ NO modifying `FileRepository.processCsvFile` conversion behavior (regression: the conversion pipeline and its tests are the app's core; upload is a separate repository)
- ❌ NO WebView in the happy path (user decision: migrate OFF webview; WebView stays only in the existing help dialog)
- ❌ NO porting the garth OAuth1a flow and NO using existing JVM libraries (research: garth login dead since 2026-03; every JVM port found implements the dead flow)
- ❌ NO logging secrets — `Authorization`, password, MFA code, `refresh_token` redacted before any Log call (security)
- ❌ NO hardcoded UI strings — every new string in both `values/strings.xml` and `values-ru/strings.xml` (repo convention)
- ❌ NO real network calls in unit tests (hermeticity: MockWebServer only)
- ❌ NO TODO stubs in the auth/upload core flow (completeness)

## Approach

Port the DI OAuth2 authentication of python-garminconnect 0.3.x (the local reference fork at ~/WebstormProjects/python-garminconnect, v0.3.17) to a Kotlin `garmin/` package: mobile login strategy (with SSO-widget HTML-form fallback), `NeedsMfa` state + `resumeLogin(code)`, service ticket → `diauth.garmin.com` token exchange, JWT-exp-based refresh, token validation against `socialProfile`. Records are encoded with the official Garmin fit-java-sdk as weight_scale messages (weight, percent fat, BMI) and uploaded as one batched multipart FIT per conversion to `/upload-service/upload`; the response's `detailedImportResult` decides per-record success (journal) vs residual fallback CSV. A local timestamp journal dedupes re-shares. Every failure mode funnels into the existing Downloads+browser flow, so the app never regresses below today's UX.

Upload orchestration lives in a new `GarminRepository` wired through `MainViewModelFactory.createInstance`; `FileRepository` stays conversion-only. The login dialog is an AlertDialog with a custom view (no fragments, per app convention).

## Architecture

- `garmin/GarminAuthClient.kt` — login chain (mobile → widget), MFA, ticket→DI exchange, refresh, `socialProfile` validation; typed exceptions
- `garmin/GarminTokenStore.kt` — `{di_token, di_refresh_token, di_client_id}` AES(Keystore)-encrypted in SharedPreferences; `TokenCrypto` interface for testability
- `garmin/GarminUploadClient.kt` — FIT build via `com.garmin.fit:fit`, multipart upload, `detailedImportResult` parsing, native headers (`User-Agent: GCM-Android-5.23`, `X-Garmin-*`)
- `garmin/UploadJournal.kt` — sent-timestamp journal (JSON in private storage)
- `garmin/RedactingHttpLogger.kt` — debug-only OkHttp interceptor, TAG `GarminHttp`
- `data/GarminRepository.kt` — upload orchestration: journal filter → login/refresh → batched upload → journal/fallback decision; Dispatchers.IO
- `ui/MainViewModel.kt` + `MainActivity.kt` — upload state machine (`Idle → Uploading → Success / Partial / FallbackNeeded / LoginRequired`), "Connect Garmin" action, login AlertDialog
- `app/build.gradle` — add okhttp (+ mockwebserver for tests, + `com.garmin.fit:fit`)
- Data flow: share CSV → `processCsvFile` (unchanged) → journal filter → login if needed → batched FIT upload → success: journal + status; failure: residual CSV via `GarminCsvSchema.formatRecord` → Downloads → browser import
- Timezone: Tefal exports local time without TZ; FIT timestamps converted to UTC using the device timezone (documented limitation)

## Design Rationale

### Problem

Today the app converts a Tefal Goodvibes CSV into a Garmin CSV, saves it to Downloads and opens the Garmin Connect web import page after 1.5 s — the user then uploads the file, picks units and clicks import by hand. The goal is a fully automated import: after conversion the data lands in Garmin Connect by itself, with UI only for the one-time Garmin authorization.

### Research Findings

**Codebase (tefal2garmin):**
- `MainActivity.kt:293-328` — `saveFileAutomatically` writes to public Downloads, schedules browser open at +1.5 s; `MainActivity.kt:330-342` — `openGarminConnect` ACTION_VIEW intent; URL constant `MainViewModel.kt:39`
- `FileRepository.kt:37-114` — `processCsvFile` returns `CsvProcessingResult` with parsed records + full `csvData` on Dispatchers.IO; natural post-conversion hook
- `MainViewModel.kt:179-200` — `MainViewModelFactory.createInstance` manual DI chain; new repository slots in here
- `AndroidManifest.xml:13-14` — INTERNET permission already present; no cleartext config (HTTPS-only enforced)
- `app/build.gradle:59-79` — NO HTTP client, NO MockWebServer, NO security libs today; coroutines 1.7.3 present
- `strings.xml` / `values-ru/strings.xml` — 47 keys each, verified in sync; new strings follow the comment-section pattern
- WebView exists only for the help dialog (`MainActivity.kt:370-406`), javaScriptEnabled=false

**Reference implementation (python-garminconnect fork, local copy v0.3.17, 2026-09-29):**
- `client.py:475-605` — 5-strategy login chain; only credential errors abort; per-strategy 429 fall-through; token verified against `GET /userprofile-service/socialProfile` (`client.py:421-447`)
- `client.py:1317-1380` — `POST diauth.{domain}/di-oauth2-service/oauth/token` service-ticket grant → `di_token` + `di_refresh_token` + `di_client_id`; `client.py:1432-1506` — JWT-exp refresh (900 s window) + one 401→refresh→retry per request
- `client.py:1153-1266` — MFA `verifyCode` (portal + mobile endpoints tried separately); `__init__.py:1098` — `resume_login(client_state, mfa_code)`; no standalone resend — code delivery re-triggered by re-running the widget request
- `__init__.py:1404-1446` — `add_body_composition(timestamp, weight, percent_fat, ..., bmi)` = FIT (weight_scale, global mesg 30) → multipart `POST /upload-service/upload`; field scales: weight/fat ×100, bmi ×10
- `__init__.py:1449-1519` — `add_weigh_in` JSON `POST /weight-service/user-weight` (weight only)
- `__init__.py:411-511` — retry decorator: 3 attempts, 5xx/transport only, backoff `min(10s, 1s·2^n)·(0.5+rand(0.5))`; 401/429 fail fast
- `client.py:1718-1727` — `detailedImportResult.failures[0].messages[0]` error extraction

**External (internet research, 2026-10-14):**
- garth is dead: `sso.garmin.com/mobile/api/login` returns Cloudflare 429 since 2026-03-17 even for plain curl (github.com/matin/garth issue #217, discussion #222); garth deprecated 2026-06
- python-garminconnect survived by dropping garth in 0.3.0 (github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect issue #332); ecosystem breakage continued (#444 Sept: valid DI token got 403 — TLS-fingerprint-based rejection, plain `requests` rejected, curl_cffi passes; #453 Oct: 429 on first request)
- NO maintained JVM/Kotlin port exists: Garmin-Client (Java, 2021), kacirekj/garmin-api (2022), floste7/garmin-connect-client (repo gone), garmin4j (vanished) — all dead or garth-era. A Kotlin port is greenfield on the 0.3.x contract
- Client IDs / headers verified from source: login `GCM_IOS_DARK` browser-UA; exchange Basic-auth ladder `GARMIN_CONNECT_MOBILE_ANDROID_DI_2025Q2` → `_2024Q4` → `_ANDROID_DI` → `_IOS_DI`; API headers `User-Agent: GCM-Android-5.23`, `X-Garmin-User-Agent: com.garmin.android.apps.connectmobile/5.23...`, `X-App-Ver: 10861`, `X-Garmin-Client-Platform: Android`, `X-GCExperience: GC5`; `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED` and CN-domain `invalid_grant` handled explicitly in the fork
- Official Garmin Health API is partner-only and read-only (developer.garmin.com/gc-developer-program/health-api) — not a path for a consumer write
- FIT upload path is production-proven (github.com/sodelalbert/Withings2Garmin, same FitEncoderWeight pattern, broke only on its garth login); official fit-java-sdk (github.com/garmin/fit-java-sdk) can build the FIT on Android

### Approaches Considered

#### 1. Port python-garminconnect 0.3.x DI-auth + official fit-java-sdk ✓

**What it is:** Kotlin port of the DI OAuth2 login (mobile strategy + widget fallback, MFA, refresh) plus the official Garmin FIT SDK building weight_scale messages for the upload.

**Investigation:**
- Read the local fork's `client.py`/`__init__.py` — the wire contract is fully specified and 2 weeks old
- Verified fit-java-sdk exists and is the official FIT builder for Java/Android
- Verified the upload endpoint pattern is production-proven (Withings2Garmin)

**Pros:**
- FIT format correctness guaranteed by Garmin's own SDK (spec risk eliminated)
- Full metric set (weight + fat + BMI) meets the user's "everything Garmin accepts" requirement
- Auth modeled on the only implementation that survived the March 2026 breakage

**Cons:**
- +~1.5-2 MB dependency for one message type (accepted trade-off)
- OkHttp TLS fingerprint vs Cloudflare unverified (spike in Task 1; user chose to decide plan-B live if it fails)

**Chosen because:** lowest format risk, complete data, and the reference contract is locally available and current.

#### 2. Own mini FIT encoder (port of fit.py) ❌

**What it is:** Same DI-auth port, but a hand-written ~300-400 line FIT encoder (header + file_id + weight_scale + CRC16) with byte-golden tests against Python-generated fixtures, instead of the SDK.

**Why we looked at this:** zero extra dependencies; the app is tiny and the weight_scale message is a frozen, simple profile.

**Investigation:**
- `fit.py` FitEncoderWeight is 517 lines; a Kotlin port needs the message + CRC + endianness handling
- Withings2Garmin and python-garminconnect both hand-roll it — pattern is proven

**Pros:** no SDK dependency, smaller APK, full control.
**Cons:** self-maintained spec code (endianness, CRC16, arch-defined fields); golden fixtures must be regenerated when fields change.

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** the official SDK removes the entire spec-maintenance burden for a ~2 MB cost in a personal utility app; KISS wins.

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** APK size becomes a real constraint or the SDK proves unusable on minSdk 21.

#### 3. Weight-only JSON endpoint ❌

**What it is:** Only `POST /weight-service/user-weight` (weight, no fat/BMI), no FIT at all.

**Investigation:** endpoint verified in the fork (`__init__.py:1449-1476`), simplest possible writer.

**Pros:** minimal code.
**Cons:** loses percent fat and BMI.

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** directly violates the user's Phase 1 decision ("send everything Garmin accepts").

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** the user explicitly downgrades the metric requirement.

#### 4. WebView login + cookie/session reuse ❌

**What it is:** Log in inside a WebView, harvest session cookies, replay them for uploads (the approach sketched in the pre-brainstorm session).

**Investigation:** the user's kickoff message for this brainstorm explicitly redirects from webview to API; python-garminconnect moved away from browser flows.

**Pros:** no credential handling in-app; real browser TLS.
**Cons:** fragile scraping of Garmin HTML; keeps the webview dependency being removed.

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** contradicts the explicit task ("переведи импорт с webview на api").

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** the OkHttp TLS spike fails AND the user chooses this hybrid at that decision point (user explicitly deferred this choice to spike results).

#### 5. Existing JVM library ❌

**What it is:** Use a published Java/Kotlin Garmin client.

**Investigation (GitHub/Maven sweep):** all found candidates are abandoned (2021-2022) or implement the dead garth flow; one Maven artifact's repo is gone.

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** nothing maintained exists; using one would couple us to a dead auth flow.

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** a maintained JVM port of the 0.3.x DI flow appears.

### Scope Boundaries

**In scope:** DI auth (mobile + widget strategies, MFA, refresh), Keystore token store, dedup journal, batched FIT upload via fit-java-sdk, residual-CSV fallback, login AlertDialog, debug HTTP logging with redaction, MockWebServer test suite, live auth spike, EN/RU strings, README note on TZ assumption.

**Out of scope (deferred/never):**
- garmin.cn domain support (never requested; user chose .com only)
- Retry queue of unsent records (user rejected in Phase 1 — fallback CSV covers it)
- Server-side dedup check via read endpoints (local journal chosen)
- Metrics beyond weight/fat/BMI (Tefal CSV has nothing else)
- Garmin Health/partner API (read-only, partner-only)
- Portal login strategy (3rd strategy) — only if both mobile and widget fail in the spike
- garth/OAuth1a anything (dead flow)

### Open Questions

- Will OkHttp's TLS fingerprint pass Cloudflare on login and API calls? → answered by Task 1 live spike; plan-B decision consciously deferred by the user
- Does `upload-service/upload` accept a multi-record weight_scale FIT (spec-valid, single-record proven)? → verify in the upload task; if rejected, degrade to per-record uploads with a small delay
- Actual refresh-token lifetime on the DI flow (server-provided; monitor during spike)
- Does Garmin surface the BMI field from weight_scale in Connect UI? → verify during spike/manual test

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)

> Preserved from the brainstorming session (2026-10-14, 3 Socratic rounds) for task creation and obstacle handling.

### Key Decisions Made

| Question | User Answer | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Upload trigger | Auto-upload right after conversion | No browser in happy path; upload starts in background after conversion success |
| API failure behavior | CSV fallback (Downloads + browser) | Web import flow retained as fallback path only |
| Partial failure (28/30) | Residual CSV: fallback contains only unuploaded records | Journal written per-record from import result |
| Login model | One-time interactive garth-style login; store only refresh token | No password storage; MFA at login time |
| Token storage | Manual Keystore AES + SharedPreferences; NO androidx.security (deprecated) | `TokenCrypto` interface for testability |
| Dedup | Local journal of sent timestamps | No extra read-API dependency |
| CSV on success | Do NOT write to Downloads on success | Downloads stays clean; file only on failure |
| Login UI | Both: "Connect Garmin" button upfront AND auto-prompt on first CSV without token | Two trigger paths into the same dialog |
| Metrics | Everything Garmin accepts | weight + fat + BMI → weight_scale FIT |
| MFA | Full support (code entry + re-trigger) | NeedsMfa state + resume; resend = re-run widget trigger |
| Garmin domains | .com only | No is_cn branching, simpler client |
| Debug tooling | Full HTTP logs in debug, secrets redacted | `RedactingHttpLogger`, TAG GarminHttp |
| Retry queue | Rejected | Fallback CSV is the failure path, no queued retries |
| Implementation approach | fit-java-sdk (official) over own encoder | +2 MB dep accepted for spec safety |
| TLS kill-switch | Decide later with spike data in hand | No pre-committed plan-B; revisit at spike results |

### Research Deep-Dives

#### Which auth contract to port?
**Sources:** local python-garminconnect fork v0.3.17 (`client.py` read in full by agent); matin/garth repo status + issues #217/#222; cyberjunky/python-garminconnect issues #332/#444/#453.
**Findings:** garth's OAuth1a mobile flow is dead (Cloudflare 429 since 2026-03-17); the 0.3.x DI OAuth2 flow (mobile login → service ticket → diauth token exchange) is the only surviving contract; rejection is TLS-fingerprint-based, not only IP-based; CN accounts refresh via diauth.garmin.cn only.
**Conclusion:** port 0.3.x exactly; implement mobile + widget strategies; validate tokens via socialProfile before acceptance; never retry 429.

#### How to carry fat% and BMI?
**Sources:** fork `__init__.py:1404-1446` + `fit.py` (FitEncoderWeight, weight_scale mesg 30, scales ×100/×10); garmin/fit-java-sdk repo; sodelalbert/Withings2Garmin production usage.
**Findings:** JSON endpoint carries weight only; fat/BMI exist only in the FIT path; the official Java SDK can build the same message on Android.
**Conclusion:** fit-java-sdk + multipart upload; one batched FIT per conversion (open question: multi-record acceptance).

#### Is there anything to reuse on JVM?
**Sources:** GitHub repo search (java/kotlin), Maven Central, mvnrepository.
**Findings:** Garmin-Client (10★, 2021), kacirekj/garmin-api (4★, 2022), floste7 artifact (repo gone), garmin4j (vanished); ecosystem alive only in Python/C#/Go/Dart — all non-Python on the dead garth flow except dotnet/garmin-connect (C#).
**Conclusion:** greenfield Kotlin port of the 0.3.x contract.

### Dead-End Paths

#### garth / OAuth1a flow
**Why explored:** garth was the canonical Garmin auth library for years ("worked 2.5 years almost without issues").
**Investigation:** garminconnect #332 — `oauth-service/oauth/preauthorized` 401 since 2026-03-17; garth discussion #222 — deprecation announced, mobile login Cloudflare-429'd even for bare curl.
**Why abandoned:** the flow cannot complete fresh logins at all; tokens from before March 2026 still work but new ones cannot be obtained.

#### Existing JVM libraries
**Why explored:** a ready-made Java/Kotlin client would eliminate the port.
**Investigation:** full GitHub/Maven sweep — everything abandoned or garth-era (see above).
**Why abandoned:** no maintained implementation of the surviving DI contract exists.

#### WebView cookie-reuse hybrid
**Why explored:** it was the leading candidate in the pre-brainstorm session (memory obs #923) — real browser TLS would pass Cloudflare.
**Investigation:** user's kickoff command explicitly redirected "from webview to API"; scraping-based session capture is fragile.
**Why abandoned:** contradicts the explicit task; kept only as a potential plan-B if the TLS spike fails, per the user's deferral.

#### Official Garmin Health API
**Why explored:** official beats unofficial for longevity.
**Investigation:** developer.garmin.com — partner program, read-only ingest (Garmin pushes TO partners), licensing fees, individual applications reportedly paused.
**Why abandoned:** cannot write weigh-ins for a consumer account.

### Open Concerns Raised

- "What if Garmin blocks OkHttp's TLS fingerprint?" → user chose to decide with spike data in hand (no pre-commitment); fallback CSV flow covers users regardless
- "What if the batched multi-record FIT is rejected?" → degrade to per-record uploads (design decision deferred to the upload task)
- "What if Garmin changes the DI flow again (March 2026 repeat)?" → CSV fallback keeps the app functional; debug HTTP logs make diagnosis fast; the fork upstream remains the repair reference
- "Refresh token lifetime unknown" → spike will observe actual `exp` values; journal+fallback unaffected

title: Task 1: GarminAuthClient + live TLS spike (DI OAuth2 login)
description:
## Goal

Kill the epic's #1 risk early and lay the auth foundation: a Kotlin `GarminAuthClient` implementing the python-garminconnect 0.3.x DI OAuth2 login (mobile strategy), MFA, token exchange and refresh — plus a documented live spike proving whether OkHttp's TLS fingerprint passes Garmin's Cloudflare.

## Effort Estimate

~8 hours (deps + 5 small classes + 2 test classes + manual spike). Under the 16h breakdown threshold; cohesive around "auth core + risk spike".

## Implementation

1. Study the reference (read-only):
   - `~/WebstormProjects/python-garminconnect/garminconnect/client.py:475-605` (login chain + `serviceTicketId` extraction), `client.py:1317-1380` (ticket→DI exchange), `client.py:1432-1506` (exp-based refresh), `client.py:1153-1266` (MFA verify) and `client.py:1624` (`resume_login`), `client.py:182` (`_MFARequired` detection), `client.py:421-447` (token validation via socialProfile)
   - `app/src/main/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/ui/MainViewModel.kt:179-200` (manual DI wiring convention)
   - Wire constants (verified by research): login `POST https://sso.garmin.com/mobile/api/login` JSON `{username, password, rememberMe:false, captchaToken:""}` with client `GCM_IOS_DARK` + iPhone Safari UA; exchange `POST https://diauth.garmin.com/di-oauth2-service/oauth/token`, Basic auth `GARMIN_CONNECT_MOBILE_ANDROID_DI_2025Q2`, form `grant_type=https://connectapi.garmin.com/di-oauth2-service/oauth/grant/service_ticket&service_ticket=...&service_url=https://mobile.integration.garmin.com/gcm/ios`; refresh `grant_type=refresh_token`; validation `GET https://connectapi.garmin.com/userprofile-service/socialProfile` with `Authorization: Bearer <di_token>`, `User-Agent: GCM-Android-5.23`, `X-Garmin-User-Agent: com.garmin.android.apps.connectmobile/5.23; ; Google/sdk_gphone64_arm64/google; Android/33; Dalvik/2.1.0`, `X-App-Ver: 10861`, `X-Garmin-Client-Platform: Android`, `X-Lang: en`, `X-GCExperience: GC5`

2. Write tests FIRST (TDD, `app/src/test/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/garmin/`):
   - `GarminAuthClientTest` (MockWebServer), scenario-per-bug:
     - `login_success_returns_tokens` — mobile login → ticket → exchange → tokens; asserts exchange request body contains the service_ticket and the returned Tokens carry di_token/di_refresh_token/di_client_id
     - `login_mfa_required_returns_client_state_and_resume_completes` — login responds MFA marker → `NeedsMfa(clientState)`; `resumeLogin(code)` POSTs verifyCode and completes the exchange (catches broken state threading between phases)
     - `wrong_credentials_throw_auth_error_without_fallback_retry` — 401/credential-error response → exactly ONE login request recorded on the mock (catches hidden retry loops)
     - `rate_limited_429_surfaces_immediately_no_retry` — 429 → `GarminTooManyRequestsError`, exactly one request recorded
     - `html_challenge_response_raises_connection_error_not_json_crash` — 200/403 response with `Content-Type: text/html` and a Cloudflare challenge body → `GarminConnectionError` with "challenge/HTML" indication, no JsonParsingException escapes (catches the fingerprint-block case being misread as a parse bug)
     - `captcha_required_raises_auth_error` — response indicating CAPTCHA_REQUIRED → `GarminAuthError` mentioning captcha (catches infinite strategy loops)
     - `exchange_client_id_ladder_advances_on_400` — first exchange 400 → second request uses `GARMIN_CONNECT_MOBILE_ANDROID_DI_2024Q4` Basic auth → succeeds (catches hardcoded single client id)
     - `refresh_triggered_when_jwt_expires_within_900s` — token with exp in 600 s → refresh grant POSTed before the API call (catches never-refresh bug)
     - `api_401_refreshes_once_then_retries_once_second_401_is_auth_error` — exactly 2 API attempts + 1 refresh call (catches retry storms)
     - `blank_credentials_fail_fast_before_network` — blank email/password → `GarminAuthError`, zero requests on mock (catches wasted Cloudflare hits)
     - `unicode_password_json_encoded_utf8` — password "пароль123✓" appears correctly UTF-8-escaped in the recorded request body (catches charset bugs)
     - `socialProfile_non_200_rejects_token` — 500 on validation → login fails cleanly (catches accepting unvalidated tokens)
     - `malformed_json_response_raises_connection_error` — 200 with garbage body → typed error, no crash
   - `GarminTokenStoreTest` (Robolectric + fake `TokenCrypto`): save/load roundtrip of `{di_token, di_refresh_token, di_client_id}`; `clear()` wipes; corrupted blob → treated as absent (not a crash); crypto throws → treated as absent + error log

3. Implementation checklist:
   - [ ] `app/build.gradle` — add `com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp:4.12.0`, testImpl `com.squareup.okhttp3:mockwebserver:4.12.0` (verify exact latest 4.x via context7 before pinning)
   - [ ] `garmin/GarminExceptions.kt` — `GarminAuthError`, `GarminTooManyRequestsError`, `GarminConnectionError`, `GarminNotFoundError` (mirror fork's `exceptions.py`); all carry a human-readable detail
   - [ ] `garmin/GarminAuthClient.kt` — `suspend fun login(email, password): LoginResult` where `LoginResult = Tokens | NeedsMfa(clientState)`; `suspend fun resumeLogin(clientState, code): Tokens`; `suspend fun refreshIfNeeded(tokens): Tokens`; internal ticket→DI exchange with client-id ladder (2025Q2 → 2024Q4 → ANDROID_DI → IOS_DI on 400/401, max 4 attempts); `socialProfile` validation; JWT `exp` read by Base64-decoding the unverified JWT payload (no crypto library — parse only, wrap in runCatcher; malformed JWT → force refresh); OkHttp on Dispatchers.IO; call timeout 15 s (mirror fork); per-class TAG logging of stages only
   - [ ] Retry scope: NO retry on login/MFA/exchange calls; retry (3 attempts, backoff `min(10s, 1s·2^n)·(0.5+rand(0.5))`) applies only to post-auth API GET (socialProfile). 429 and auth errors are never retried anywhere
   - [ ] `garmin/TokenCrypto.kt` — interface + `KeystoreAesCrypto` impl (AndroidKeyStore AES/GCM key, `javax.crypto.Cipher`); keystore unavailable/corrupt → throws typed `TokenCryptoException`
   - [ ] `garmin/GarminTokenStore.kt` — encrypt-then-persist via `SharedPreferences` (`garmin_di_tokens` key); on `TokenCryptoException` → return "no tokens" + Log.w (fail-safe to LoginRequired, never crash)
   - [ ] `garmin/RedactingHttpLogger.kt` — debug-only OkHttp interceptor (guarded by `BuildConfig.DEBUG`, zero-op in release), TAG `GarminHttp`, logs method/URL/status/bodies, redacts values of `Authorization`, `password`, `mfaVerificationCode`, `refresh_token`, `service_ticket`, `di_token` keys
   - [ ] NO production UI in this task — a temporary debug-only entry point (e.g. hidden long-press action) is acceptable to drive the live spike; the login dialog is a later task

4. Live spike (manual, debug build, real account):
   - Run login with a real Garmin account (MFA if enabled). Interpret results by CATEGORY, not by single response:
     - JSON success → PASS
     - Single 429 (JSON or header) → rate limit: wait ≥10 minutes, retry ONCE; two consecutive 429s → report as INCONCLUSIVE-429, not FAIL
     - 403 with `text/html` Cloudflare challenge (or non-JSON HTML on login) → likely TLS-fingerprint block → FAIL candidate; retry once after 10 min to confirm
     - CAPTCHA_REQUIRED → report as separate finding (implies captcha challenge, not necessarily fingerprint)
   - Record observed token `exp` lifetime from the DI JWT
   - Capture a redacted log excerpt; `adb logcat | grep -iE "password|di_token|refresh|ticket"` (case-insensitive) over the captured window must show no secret VALUE (key names in redaction markers are fine)
   - Record verdict + excerpt via `br comments add` on this issue; if FAIL — STOP and report to the user; plan-B (e.g. WebView hybrid) is explicitly the user's deferred decision, do NOT implement it autonomously

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All new unit tests pass: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.example.tefal2garmin.garmin.*"` — 13+ GarminAuthClientTest scenarios + 4 GarminTokenStoreTest scenarios green
- [ ] Full suite + lint green: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug` — no regressions in the existing 47-string/pipeline tests
- [ ] Live spike documented in issue comments: verdict (PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE-429 / CAPTCHA), redacted log excerpt, observed token lifetime
- [ ] Secret-scan clean: grep over captured spike logcat shows no credential/token/ticket values; release build contains a zero-op logger (assert via code review — no bodies logged when BuildConfig.DEBUG=false)
- [ ] Request-count guarantees verified by tests: wrong-creds=1 request, 429=1 request, 401-on-API=2 requests+1 refresh (prevents retry storms against Garmin)

## Key Considerations (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

**Cloudflare HTML challenges (the fingerprint case)**: Garmin responds 200/403 with an HTML challenge instead of JSON when it dislikes the client. MUST check Content-Type/first-byte before JSON parsing; HTML → `GarminConnectionError("challenge")`. This is the single most likely real-world failure of the spike — misclassifying it as a JSON parse bug would corrupt the spike verdict.

**Blank/garbage input**: blank email or password fail-fast client-side, zero network (every wasted request is rate-limit exposure).

**Non-ASCII credentials**: Russian-language passwords are likely for this user; UTF-8 JSON encoding of the login body is test-verified.

**Refresh-token death**: refresh 400 `invalid_grant` → `GarminAuthError` → token store cleared → LoginRequired. Never loop refresh.

**Clock skew**: JWT exp checks use the device clock; a badly wrong clock may cause premature/late refresh — acceptable (worst case one extra refresh), documented here, no server-time compensation in this task.

**Keystore unavailability**: rare broken Keystores must degrade to "no tokens" + Log.w, not crash the app.

**Concurrency**: single-user sequential flow; no locking needed yet. Later GarminRepository serializes upload vs login (noted for the next task).

**Retry discipline**: 429/401-cred are never retried (epic anti-pattern); backoff only for 5xx/transport on API GETs.

## Anti-Patterns

Inherited from epic `tefal2garmin-garmin-api-import-j5e` (all apply). Task-specific:
- ❌ NO storing email/password anywhere, ever (only DI tokens via GarminTokenStore)
- ❌ NO retry loops on login/429/auth errors (request-count assertions in tests enforce this)
- ❌ NO JSON parsing without Content-Type/challenge guard (Cloudflare HTML must map to GarminConnectionError)
- ❌ NO TODO stubs in auth flow — NeedsMfa/resume/ladder must be real implementations with tests
- ❌ NO secrets in logs — redaction list: Authorization, password, mfaVerificationCode, refresh_token, service_ticket, di_token
- ❌ NO crash paths from malformed remote data — all parses wrapped, typed exceptions escape

## Goal

Build the epic's data plane: encode weight + percent-fat + BMI records into a weight_scale FIT file with the official Garmin FIT Java SDK, batch-upload it to the unofficial `/upload-service/upload` endpoint, parse `detailedImportResult` per-record outcomes — plus the local dedup journal that decides which records are new.

## Effort Estimate

~8 hours (2 main classes + journal + ~18 test scenarios + dependency). Under the 16h threshold; independent of the pending live TLS spike (MockWebServer is hermetic).

## Implementation

1. Study (read-only):
   - `~/WebstormProjects/python-garminconnect/garminconnect/__init__.py:1404-1446` (`add_body_composition`: FIT build → multipart POST), `fit.py` FitEncoderWeight (field scales: weight/percent_fat ×100, bmi ×10, timestamp field 253), `client.py:1645-1739` (`_run_request`: multipart file handling, 204/400 handling, `detailedImportResult.failures[0].messages[0]` extraction at `client.py:1718-1727`)
   - Existing task-1 code in `app/src/main/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/garmin/` (GarminAuthClient — its refresh + native-header logic; RedactingHttpLogger; exceptions) — REUSE, don't duplicate. If needed, extract a package-internal shared request helper from GarminAuthClient (keep all 20 existing tests green — they are the refactor safety net)
   - FIT Java SDK usage: dependency `com.garmin:fit:21.176.0` (verified latest on Maven Central; plain Java 8, works with D8/minSdk 21). Encoding pattern per cookbook: https://developer.garmin.com/fit/cookbook/encoding-activity-files/ (BufferEncoder or Encoder + FileIdMesg + WeightScaleMesg; `com.garmin.fit.DateTime` from java.util.Date UTC). Decode for tests: `Decoder` + MesgListener. VERIFY exact setter names/scaling semantics from the SDK sources jar ( IntelliJ: download sources) — do not guess
   - Wire format: `POST https://connectapi.garmin.com/upload-service/upload`, multipart part name `file`, filename `body_composition.fit`, same native headers as task 1 (Bearer di_token, `User-Agent: GCM-Android-5.23`, `X-Garmin-User-Agent`, `X-App-Ver: 10861`, `X-Garmin-Client-Platform: Android`, `X-Lang: en`, `X-GCExperience: GC5`)

2. Write tests FIRST (`app/src/test/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/garmin/`, plain JUnit + JVM seams — Robolectric is broken on this JDK-26 toolchain, do not use):
   - `GarminUploadClientTest` (MockWebServer):
     - `multipart_request_shape_and_native_headers` — part name `file`, filename `body_composition.fit`, Bearer + GCM headers present
     - `fit_roundtrip_weight_fat_bmi_decoded` — captured multipart bytes decoded with SDK `Decoder`; WeightScaleMesg fields match input (catches wrong mesg type/scaling)
     - `fit_multiple_records_batched` — 3 records → 3 decoded weight_scale messages, each timestamp correct UTC
     - `missing_fields_omitted_from_fit` — record with null percentFat/bmi → decoded mesg has those fields unset (catches encoding garbage zeros)
     - `response_all_success_returns_success_count`
     - `response_with_failures_returns_partial_with_messages` — `detailedImportResult.failures[]` → `Partial` with messages; when failure entries carry no correlatable record index, `succeededKeys` MUST be empty (conservative — see Key Considerations)
     - `out_of_range_weight_rejected_before_network` — weight 0 / 700 kg, fat 150%, bmi 0 → typed validation error, 0 requests on mock
     - `empty_records_returns_success_zero_without_network` — 0 requests (rate-limit hygiene)
     - `upload_429_surfaces_after_single_request` — exactly 1 request
     - `upload_401_refreshes_once_retries_once` — 2 upload attempts + 1 refresh; second 401 → GarminAuthError
     - `upload_5xx_retries_3_attempts_then_connection_error` — exactly 3 requests, backoff respected (inject fake sleeper/clock seam)
     - `html_challenge_response_maps_to_connection_error` — text/html 200/403 → GarminConnectionError, no JSON crash
     - `malformed_json_success_response_maps_to_connection_error` — 200 with garbage body → typed error
   - `UploadJournalTest` (in-memory `JournalPersistence` fake):
     - `empty_journal_all_records_new`
     - `marked_records_filtered_out`
     - `persistence_roundtrip_via_seam` — save/load preserves marked set
     - `duplicate_timestamps_within_one_batch_deduped` — two records with same timestamp in ONE input list → filterNew returns it once (catches double-upload of duplicate rows)
     - `partial_marking_then_filter` — mark 2 of 3 → next filter returns only the third

3. Implementation checklist:
   - [ ] `app/build.gradle` — `implementation 'com.garmin:fit:21.176.0'`
   - [ ] `garmin/GarminWeighInRecord.kt` — data class: `epochSecondsUtc: Long`, `weightKg: Float`, `percentFat: Float?`, `bmi: Float?`; companion `validateRanges()` (0 < weight ≤ 500 kg, 0 ≤ fat ≤ 100, 0 < bmi ≤ 100) throwing typed `GarminValidationError` (add to GarminExceptions.kt)
   - [ ] `garmin/FitWeightFileBuilder.kt` — records → FIT bytes via SDK (FileIdMesg: type WEIGHT + timeCreated; one WeightScaleMesg per record; UTC DateTime); range-validate BEFORE encode; null fat/bmi → field simply not set
   - [ ] `garmin/GarminUploadClient.kt` — `suspend fun uploadWeighIns(records, tokens): UploadResult`; sealed `UploadResult { Success(count); Partial(succeededKeys, failureMessages) }` (transport/auth/429/5xx-exhausted surface as typed exceptions, NOT result values — mirrors task 1); retry semantics identical to task 1 (5xx/transport only, 3 attempts jittered backoff; 401 → one refresh via GarminAuthClient → one retry; 429/auth never retried); multipart via OkHttp MultipartBody; parse `detailedImportResult`
   - [ ] `garmin/UploadJournal.kt` — `filterNew(records): List<GarminWeighInRecord>` (dedupes against journal AND within batch), `markSent(epochSecondsUtc: List<Long>)`, `sentCount()`; keys = epoch-second UTC strings; JSON array persisted through `JournalPersistence` seam (impl: `filesDir/upload_journal.json`); synchronized (single-process safety); corrupted JSON → start fresh + Log.w
   - [ ] NO UI, NO integration into FileRepository/ViewModel — wiring is the next task. NO changes to task-1 behavior except an extracted shared request helper (tests must stay green)

4. Verification commands (capture exit codes): `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.example.tefal2garmin.garmin.*"`, full `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`, `./gradlew lintDebug`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] 18+ new test scenarios green (13 upload + 5 journal); full suite green (140 existing + new); lintDebug no NEW errors
- [ ] FIT roundtrip proven: decoded WeightScaleMesg values match inputs exactly (weight/fat ×100, bmi ×10 scales handled by SDK) for single and multi-record batches
- [ ] Range-violating records rejected with 0 network requests; empty list → 0 network requests
- [ ] Retry discipline proven by request-count assertions: 429=1, 401=2+1 refresh, 5xx=3
- [ ] No minSdk/compileSdk changes; no new Android permissions; `com.garmin:fit:21.176.0` is the only new runtime dependency

## Key Considerations (SRE REVIEW)

**FIT scale limits**: weight_scale fields are uint16 (weight/fat scale 100 → max 655.35; bmi scale 10 → max 6553.5). SDK may silently truncate out-of-range floats — MUST range-validate in GarminWeighInRecord BEFORE encoding (human-plausible bounds above are stricter than wire limits on purpose).

**Per-record correlation uncertainty**: Garmin's `detailedImportResult.failures[]` may not carry record indices correlatable to our batch. Conservative rule: any failure indication → Partial with EMPTY succeededKeys unless indices are explicit and parseable; the integration task will journal only succeededKeys and route everything else to the residual CSV. Never guess success.

**Intra-batch duplicates**: Tefal exports can contain repeated timestamps (re-measurements); filterNew dedupes within the batch too, or the same reading uploads twice.

**Empty input**: after journal filtering the new-record list may be empty — the client must short-circuit with Success(0) and ZERO network calls (every unnecessary request is rate-limit exposure).

**Multipart bodies**: OkHttp MultipartBody builds the part; captured bytes for roundtrip tests come from a MockWebServer DiskFileUpload/RecordedRequest.getBody — read via Buffer clone, not one-shot stream.

**Thread-safety**: UploadJournal synchronized — later the upload coroutine and potential UI reads may overlap.

- ❌ NO journaling on unconfirmed success — only Success or explicit succeededKeys of Partial may be marked
- ❌ NO per-record upload loops in this task — batched FIT only (per-record mode is a documented plan-B, not default)

- ❌ NO touching .beads/, CRUSH.md, or task-1 test expectations
- ❌ NO minSdk/permission/dependency changes beyond com.garmin:fit:21.176.0

title: Task 3: GarminRepository orchestration (data layer)
description:
## Goal

Data-layer orchestration: parse the produced Garmin CSV, dedup via journal, drive login/refresh/upload through the task-1/2 clients, and produce residual fallback CSV — behind one interface the UI task consumes in parallel.

## SHARED CONTRACT (verbatim — the UI task codes against THIS; do not rename)

```kotlin
// app/src/main/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/data/GarminRepository.kt
sealed class LoginStatus {
    object Success : LoginStatus()
    object NeedsMfa : LoginStatus()
    data class Failed(val reason: String) : LoginStatus()
}
sealed class UploadOutcome {
    object NotNeeded : UploadOutcome()
    data class Success(val uploadedCount: Int) : UploadOutcome()
    data class Partial(val uploadedCount: Int, val residualCsv: String, val residualCount: Int, val messages: List<String>) : UploadOutcome()
    data class Fallback(val residualCsv: String, val residualCount: Int, val reason: String) : UploadOutcome()
    object LoginRequired : UploadOutcome()
}
interface GarminUploadOrchestrator {
    suspend fun login(email: String, password: String, mfaCode: String? = null): LoginStatus
    suspend fun uploadNewFromCsv(csvData: String): UploadOutcome
    fun hasStoredToken(): Boolean
}
class GarminRepository(context: Context) : GarminUploadOrchestrator
// plus an internal constructor taking fake collaborators for tests
```

## Semantics (binding)

- `login`: GarminAuthClient.login → NeedsMfa? if mfaCode!=null → resumeLogin; Success → GarminTokenStore.save; every exception → LoginStatus.Failed(reason). NEVER throws.
- `uploadNewFromCsv`: parse input (Garmin-format CSV: skip first `Body` line + `Date,Weight,Fat,BMI` header; read GarminCsvSchema + CsvFieldMapper for exact date/value conventions; convert Date → epochSecondsUtc using device-default timezone — documented epic limitation) → records → journal.filterNew → empty ⇒ NotNeeded (ZERO network) → !hasStoredToken ⇒ LoginRequired → validateRanges (violation ⇒ Fallback with all unmarked) → uploadWeighIns → Success: markSent(all), return Success(count) → Partial: markSent(succeededKeys), residualCsv = `Body`+header+unmarked rows via GarminCsvSchema.formatRecord, return Partial → GarminTooManyRequests/GarminConnectionError ⇒ Fallback(residual of all unmarked, reason) → GarminAuthError ⇒ clear tokens + LoginRequired. NEVER throws.
- Partial residual counts must satisfy uploadedCount + residualCount == newRecordCount.

## Files (ONLY these)

- NEW `app/src/main/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/data/GarminRepository.kt`
- NEW `app/src/test/java/com/example/tefal2garmin/data/GarminRepositoryTest.kt` (plain JUnit + fakes — Robolectric broken on JDK26)

## Tests (name-per-bug, fake collaborators)

`login_success_stores_tokens`, `login_needs_mfa_then_resume_with_code`, `login_wrong_password_returns_failed`, `login_transport_error_returns_failed_not_throw`;
`upload_not_needed_when_journal_covers_all` (0 client calls), `upload_login_required_when_no_token`, `upload_success_marks_journal_and_returns_count`, `upload_partial_marks_only_succeeded_and_residual_has_rest` (assert counts identity + residual parses back to unmarked rows), `upload_429_returns_fallback_with_all_unmarked`, `upload_transport_exhausted_returns_fallback`, `upload_auth_error_clears_token_and_returns_login_required`, `upload_range_violation_returns_fallback_zero_network`, `garmin_csv_parsing_matches_schema` (dates incl. Russian-source normalization path, comma decimals — follow GarminCsvSchema tests for fixtures).

## Anti-Patterns

Inherited from epic + task: ❌ NO throws across the interface; ❌ NO journaling unconfirmed records; ❌ NO touching garmin/, ui/, utils/, FileRepository, manifest; ❌ NO retry loops (clients already own retries); ❌ NO TODO stubs.

- [ ] Zero-network paths (NotNeeded, LoginRequired, range-violation) asserted via fake call counters

title: Task 6: Remediation — review findings (MFA deadlock, races, IO, fallback save) + hardening
description:
## Goal

Fix everything found by the end-of-epic reviews (quality CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR, security LOW, test-audit HIGH gaps) and the on-device E2E (fallback save silent failure). One pass, prioritized; production bugs first.

## Findings being fixed (sources: quality review 2026-10-14, security scan, test-effectiveness audit, E2E on device 39261FDJG004CJ)

### A. Production bugs (fix FIRST)

1. **CRITICAL — MFA deadlock.** `GarminRepository.login` always calls `remote.login(email,password)`; real `GarminAuthClient.login` throws "MFA login already in progress" when `pendingMfa != null` (GarminAuthClient.kt:93-97). After MFA_REQUIRED the code entry and resend are permanently dead. Fix: repository remembers `clientState` when login returns NeedsMfa; `login(email, pass, mfaCode)` with mfaCode!=null AND stored state → `remote.resumeLogin(clientState, mfaCode)`; resend path (mfaCode==null, state exists) → re-run `remote.login` ONLY after `remote.logout()` (or expose a resendMfa on the client — pick the smaller change, keep GarminAuthClient's gate intact). REGRESSION TEST REQUIRED: make the test fake STATEFUL (model the pendingMfa gate exactly like the real client: second login() while pending → throw) — the stateless fake is why this shipped.
2. **MAJOR — login-cancel race** (MainViewModel.kt:258-290): `loginToGarmin` stores its Job; `onLoginCancelled` cancels it and clears `pendingUploadCsv` — no late Success may run `performUpload` after fallback shipped. Test: cancel while login coroutine suspended → no upload call, no state flip.
3. **MAJOR — cancel-path residual not journal-filtered** (MainViewModel.kt:298-316): `onLoginCancelled`/`fallbackToResidualCsv` must ask the repository for the journal-filtered residual (add `suspend fun residualCsvFor(csvData: String): String` to GarminUploadOrchestrator? — NO interface change without updating the UI contract: instead move cancel-handling into a repository call `fallbackResidual(csvData): UploadOutcome.Fallback` that filters via journal, and use it in both ViewModel paths). Test: journal covers half the rows → residual contains only the rest.
4. **MAJOR — main-thread I/O**: wrap ALL GarminRepository public methods in `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` (Keystore crypto, commit(), journal readText/writeText currently run on Main via viewModelScope). Keep clients' internal IO as is.
5. **E2E — fallback save silently fails on API 37**: during the cancelled-dialog fallback the browser opened but NO garmin-import CSV appeared in Downloads (Oct 14), while Oct 8-13 files exist. Investigate `saveFileAutomatically` raw-File write to `getExternalStoragePublicDirectory` on API 33+ scoped storage. Fix: write via MediaStore Downloads collection on API 29+ (keep legacy path below); open the browser ONLY after a successful save (currently browser opens regardless — if save fails show the file_save_failed status and DON'T open). Test what's testable on JVM (guard logic), verify on device (orchestrator will).

### B. Hardening (security + quality minors)

6. Move `GARMINSPIKE_EMAIL/PASSWORD/MFA_CODE` buildConfigFields from `defaultConfig` to `buildTypes { debug { ... } }` in app/build.gradle (release BuildConfig must not even have the fields).
7. Clear login EditTexts (email/password/MFA) and null the Activity field refs on dialog dismiss/cancel/success.
8. `FileJournalPersistence.save` → temp file + atomic rename; corrupted load already starts fresh.
9. `lastResidualSaveKey` → survive recreation (store in ViewModel/savedState or move the save-once decision into the ViewModel outcome handling) so rotation doesn't re-save + re-open browser per rotation.
10. Release builds: GarminCsvParser's `Log.w` of raw CSV rows (health PII) → log row INDEX + reason only, never row content (or debug-gate the content).

### C. Test additions (audit Phase 1 + the deadlock pins; name-per-bug)

- `stateful_fake_mfa_code_entry_completes_via_resume` (pins finding 1 — fake now models pendingMfa gate)
- `resend_code_relogin_after_logout_completes`
- `login_cancel_cancels_inflight_job_and_skips_upload` (finding 2)
- `cancel_residual_is_journal_filtered` (finding 3)
- `upload_204_no_content_returns_success` (+requestCount==1)
- `refresh_400_invalid_grant_raises_auth_error_no_retry` (2 requests)
- `refresh_429_surfaces_immediately` (1 request)
- `range_boundaries_inclusive_maxima_accepted_just_over_rejected` (500.0 ok / 500.01 rejected, 0 requests; assert MAX_WEIGHT_KG*100 <= 65535)
- `orchestrator_exception_falls_back_to_residual` (ViewModel)
- `conversion_success_payload_exact_equality` (full two-row CSV string, not startsWith)
- `upload_200_successes_plus_unindexed_failures_yields_empty_succeeded_keys`
- `mfa_verify_request_carries_sso_session_cookie` (Set-Cookie → Cookie header asserted)
- `exchange_ladder_exhaustion_4x400_raises_auth_error` (5 requests)
- Same-day dedup: DECISION (orchestrator, user delegated): journal key becomes composite `"epochSecondsUtc:weightKg"` so a same-day second measurement with different weight uploads too (date-granular keys silently dropped it — audit HIGH #3). Implement + `same_day_second_measurement_uploads_and_identical_rerecord_deduped`.

## Anti-Patterns

Inherited + ❌ do NOT change GarminUploadOrchestrator's existing method signatures (UI depends); additive methods only; ❌ no new dependencies; ❌ no TODO stubs; ❌ tests must not weaken existing 185.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All A/B items implemented; full suite green (185 + ~14 new); lintDebug no new errors
- [ ] Stateful-fake MFA regression test FAILS against the old repository code (prove it pins the bug: temporarily revert the fix if needed, confirm red, restore)
- [ ] On-device re-verify by orchestrator: cancelled-dialog fallback now produces a real file in Downloads (MediaStore) and browser opens only after save success
- [ ] Release BuildConfig contains no GARMINSPIKE fields (inspect generated release BuildConfig or move assertions into unit test)
